newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia c/a deficit falls to 13 bln rgt in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia c/a deficit falls to 13 bln rgt in 1996.

text.p: Malaysia's current account deficit is projected to widen to 14.8 billion ringgit in 1997 against a revised 13 billion ringgit last year, Bank Negara said on Friday.
The widely watched current account deficit has been narrowing since reaching a peak of 18.7 billion ringgit in 1995.
"In 1996, the current account deficit declined as imports slowed down in line with slower economic activity," the central bank said in its annual report.

Most of the slowdown was due to a global slump in the electrical and electronics industry. Although the sector accounts for two-thirds of exports, most of the goods use a high degree of imported components.
The 1996 gap narrowed to 5.5 percent of the gross national product (GNP) against nine percent in 1995, when it had triggered concerns about overheating in the economy.
However, Bank Negara's official current account shortfall figure was higher than the 11 billion ringgit announced by Finance Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim last month.
A Bank Negara official said the central bank's estimate included 2.8 billion ringgit that foreign workers in Malaysia sent back home.
The services sector once again contributed the entire deficit, ending 1996 with a gap of 18.8 billion ringgit against 19 billion in the previous year, the report said.
Bank Negara said the contraction in the current account deficit was largely achieved due to slower growth in imports, which rose by just 2.6 percent against exports growth of 7.3 percent.
"Lumpy" items -- ships, aircraft and other other large one-off purchases -- declined in 1996 to 4.7 billion ringgit from 7.2 billion in the previous year.
However, the current account gap would increase in 1997 as imports were expected to grow at a slightly faster rate of 8.4 percent against a projected 7.2 percent growth in exports.
"In the event the recovery in the global electronics industry falters, or occurs in the latter part of the year, export growth could be lower," the report said.
